clue.text: Nehru is said to have criticized the thing

indicators.note: is said tells us the phrase is spoken, and the sound gives a different written word

parts.note: to criticize something harshly is to pan it, so 'criticized the thing' is panned it

explanation.surface: A report that India's prime minister once spoke harshly about some object.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'panned it' sounds like the title Pandit, which Jawaharlal Nehru bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was widely known by the honorific Pandit, a title for a learned Hindu scholar.

clue.text: As Miss Dombey was to Mr Toots

definitions.text: As Miss Dombey was to Mr Toots

parts.words: As Miss Dombey was to Mr Toots
parts.note: in Dickens's Dombey and Son the bashful Mr Toots worships Florence Dombey, so she seemed to him worthy of devotion

explanation.surface: How a Dickens heroine appeared to her lovestruck admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toots is besotted with Florence, finding her utterly lovable and charming.

clue.text: "Uglification and ——" in the Mock Turtle's arithmetic

definitions.text: "Uglification and ——" in the Mock Turtle's arithmetic

parts.words: "Uglification and ——" in the Mock Turtle's arithmetic
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle names the branches of arithmetic as Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and a fourth, a pun on division

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Lewis Carroll's Mock Turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's fourth branch of arithmetic puns on division with a word for scornful mockery.

clue.text: Figures are cooked — sign later

indicators.note: cooked, as accounts are cooked, says the letters are falsified into another order

explanation.surface: Accounts that are fiddled, with the signature added later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests accounts, with 'cooked' as fraud; but the figures are geometric shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are three-sided geometric figures.

clue.text: So a grass may become a weed ?:

indicators.note: may become says these letters can be turned into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A musing on whether ordinary grass could turn into a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SO A GRASS. 'Weed' here is seaweed: the Sargasso is a floating brown seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso, or gulfweed, is a floating brown seaweed giving its name to the Sargasso Sea.

clue.text: Gilbertian naval knight, dreamer and railwayman

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
Joseph in Genesis is the dreamer of dreams
a porter carries luggage at a railway station

explanation.surface: A list of three people: a sailor knight, a dreamer and a railway worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Joseph Porter is First Lord of the Admiralty in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore; 'knight' gives SIR and also finishes the picture of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Lord of the Admiralty in HMS Pinafore, the naval figure of Gilbert's comic opera.

clue.text: Devices a tribe is given

parts.note: Gad is one of the twelve tribes of Israel
gets means receives, is given

explanation.surface: Equipment handed out to a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Gad is one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgets are small mechanical contrivances or devices.

clue.text: Possibly raise log building in Turkey

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of raise log might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A builder thinking of hoisting a log for a building in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange RAISE LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, notably in Istanbul's Topkapi.

clue.text: Boss is agitated about being in Latin haunts

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the other piece
agitated says the letters of boss are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: esse is the Latin verb to be, as a noun being

explanation.surface: A boss who is anxious about something in Latin and preoccupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns BOSS into OBSS, and 'about' wraps that round ESSE: OBS-ESSE-S.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone's mind is to preoccupy them constantly, as an obsession does.

clue.text: Special messenger imbibing tea, we hear, with palace attendant

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a courier is a messenger carrying special dispatches

indicators.note: we hear says the word tea is taken by its sound, the letter name

parts.note: the drink tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A royal messenger drinking tea alongside a palace servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns tea into the letter T, which goes inside COURIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is a person in attendance at a royal court or palace.

clue.text: Decks of gold buried in sand, perhaps

indicators.note: buried in puts one piece inside the other, as treasure is buried in sand
perhaps hints that sand stands only loosely for its letters, which are rearranged

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Treasure chests of gold buried in a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SAND to ADNS, and 'buried in' puts OR inside it after AD: AD-OR-NS.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to adorn or ornament it, so decks and adorns are synonyms.

clue.text: Venetian brings fish to, wild Iona

parts.note: the bass is a common sea fish

indicators.note: wild says the letters of Iona run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Venice taking fish to a wild Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a Hebridean island; 'wild' rearranges it to ANIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassanio is the Venetian suitor of Portia in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Borders of Messina (Much Ado)

explanation.surface: The frontiers of a Sicilian city, as seen in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Much Ado About Nothing is set in Messina, Sicily, where Verges serves as Dogberry's partner in the watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Borders are edges or margins; separately, Verges is the elderly headborough of Messina in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: Make Olive produce cathedral sources of wealth

parts.note: oil is what olives are pressed to produce
Wells is an English cathedral city in Somerset, known for its cathedral

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to turn a woman named Olive into a cathedral's riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a woman's name but is the fruit; WELLS is the cathedral city in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil wells pump petroleum, a commodity that has made nations rich.

clue.text: Gentlewoman's imitation flower

parts.note: a gentlewoman is a lady, with the possessive kept
mock means imitation, as in mock turtle

explanation.surface: A fake bloom belonging to a refined woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of LADY'S drops out in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's smock, or cuckooflower, is a pale lilac meadow plant of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Irish johnnie finds the North Sea rough

indicators.note: rough, as of choppy water, says the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irishman crossing a stormy North Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges N plus SEA; 'johnnie' is old slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean is a common Irish man's name, the Irish form of John, hence an Irish johnnie.

clue.text: Pungency about air force bombardment

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: sting is sharpness or pungency
RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Sharp comment over an air force bombing raid.
explanation.walkthrough: STING goes about RAF: ST-RAF-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Strafing is attacking ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Swinburne's girl in Calydon

parts.note: points to the heroine of Swinburne's verse drama set in Calydon, the huntress of Greek myth

explanation.surface: The heroine of a Victorian poet's Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Swinburne's 1865 verse drama is titled after the swift huntress of the Calydonian boar hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntress of Greek myth who joined the Calydonian boar hunt, title heroine of Swinburne's play.

clue.text: Police work in the civil service

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Policing as a job inside government administration.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (opus, a work) goes inside CS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cops is informal slang for police officers.

clue.text: Makes pure extract from treacle an' sesame

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Purifying an extract of treacle and sesame.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to clean thoroughly or purify.

clue.text: Standard value little man put on form of speech

parts.note: par is the standard or face value
Lance is a pet form of the man's name Lancelot

explanation.surface: A small man settling on standard terms of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little man' means a shortened man's name: LANCE from Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular manner of speaking, an idiom or jargon.

clue.text: Lad hopes for a floral metamorphosis .

definitions.text: Lad hopes for a floral metamorphosis

indicators.note: metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters are transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy wishing he could be turned into a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange LAD HOPES; the whole clue is the definition too, since the change yields a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, so the boy's floral transformation would yield one.

clue.text: Fire supporter-soon free to go back inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: to go back means the word free is read backwards

parts.note: rid means free, as in rid of

explanation.surface: Someone supporting a fire soon goes back in free.
explanation.walkthrough: RID is turned to DIR and placed inside ANON: AN-DIR-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal stand holding logs in a fireplace, also called a firedog.

clue.text: Refer to everything due for alteration

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: for alteration says the word due is to be changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A tailor's note pointing out that every garment is due to be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to mention or hint at it indirectly.

clue.text: Impediment to racial progress

parts.note: reads like a social barrier to an ethnic group, but means a hurdle or barrier set in a race, slowing the runners

explanation.surface: A barrier holding back the advancement of a people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racial' is used playfully to mean 'in a race': an obstacle race has barriers to be climbed.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a hindrance, such as the barriers in an obstacle race.

clue.text: Take no notice of a soldier returning to the sandbank

indicators.note: returning means the word for soldier is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the Nore is a sandbank at the mouth of the Thames estuary

explanation.surface: Ignoring a soldier who comes back to a sandbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nore is a sandbank where the Thames meets the North Sea, once a naval anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard someone is to pay them no attention at all.

clue.text: Number one of those slain by Saul

definitions.text: one of those slain by Saul

explanation.surface: A tally of one of King Saul's victims.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible says 'Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands' (1 Samuel 18:7).
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral meaning ten hundred; and Saul's victims were counted in such units in the biblical song.

clue.text: Hot kind of group contains artist or composer

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: ginger is hot and spicy, and a ginger group is a pressure group within a party
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A spicy band holding an artist or musical composer.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginger group is a British term for a faction pushing a party to act; it holds RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Grainger was an Australian-born composer and pianist, known for Country Gardens.

clue.text: Show what is written in the stars

definitions.text: what is written in the stars

explanation.surface: Demonstrate what the horoscope foretells.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a stage musical; the word also means fate, the destiny astrologers read in the stars.
